text:
oncall-bot: Pager duty: multiple NotReady transitions in inference-usw-1 pool (severity: P1). Automated mitigation kicked. 

ashley: seeing ~6 nodes flip to NotReady in the last 2m, traffic error-rate spike on routing. can someone grab kubelet logs? :pager:

lee: I'm on it, tailing kubelet on node infer-usw-1-23: `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 -f`

lee: initial suspicion: hardware watchdog triggered `kernel: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup` then `systemd: watchdog timeout, killing pid` followed by kubelet restart loop. copying dmesg snippets:
```
[ 1234.567890] watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#2 stuck for 23s!
[ 1234.568001] Kernel panic - not syncing: watchdog detected
[ 1234.568200] init: systemd watchdog timeout, killing process 1024 (kubelet)
```

tom: that's interesting — we saw similar pattern last year but with GPU drivers stuck, causing driver reset. any CUDA oops? check `dmesg | grep -i cuda` and `nvidia-smi -q`

rosa: `dmesg | grep -i nvrm` shows `NVRM: Xid 31` on two of the nodes, plus `oom-killer` activity. logs attached to incident.

mike: adding context: affected nodes are all in the same rack / hw batch, same BIOS revision. might be thermal or firmware watchdog.

ashley: customer impact: a subset of requests to hosted inference are failing with 502 due to backend timeouts; traffic retries route to fallback but we saw capacity pressure and throttling. alerting product and support.

support-bot: Created ticket CC-1248 for impacted customers, posting known issue blurb to status page draft.

lee: mitigation plan proposed: 1) cordon + drain nodes that are flapping; 2) scale up dedicated fallback pool by +30% (if capacity available); 3) enable model fallback to smaller quantized variant for high-latency paths; 4) investigate firmware and driver crash signature.

ashley: executing step 1 now: `kubectl cordon infer-usw-1-23 && kubectl drain infer-usw-1-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`

lee: node drained, pods terminating. observed a few runtime container crashes during SIGTERM with jvm-ish stack traces? runtime logs show `cudaSetDevice() failed: unspecified launch failure` before termination.

tom: runbook check — do we need to evict stateful components manually? inference runtime should checkpoint KV caches; but we might want to force-remove pods to speed recovery: `kubectl delete pod <pod> --grace-period=0 --force` if they hang.

rosa: issuing force deletes on 3 stuck pods. traffic levels are dropping on those nodes.

mike: starting autoscaler bump on dedicated pool: `terraform apply -var='scale_dedicated=+3'` (will proxy through infra pipeline). ETA ~3m for extra instances to register.

ashley: while infra scales, activate routing policy: shift new sessions away from usw-1 region for 5m window to reduce customer latency impact. ops-console: set prefer-region=usw-2 for new connections.

oncall-bot: Incident: inference-usw-1 - hardware watchog restarts -> node NotReady. Incident channel created: #incidents/4812340000.

lee: quick debug: collecting `kubectl describe node infer-usw-1-23` output and kubelet logs. noticing `RuntimeClass` eviction messages referencing `nvidia.com/gpu` and `kubelet: container runtime error: container killed due to OOM`. We have a cascade: GPU driver Xid -> kernel watchdog -> kubelet restart -> pods killed -> OOM events during restart.

tom: could be driver memory leak under specific model load. can we repro on a spare node with same BIOS + driver? I'll schedule repro in staging with same model load generator.

rosa: driver versions: 525.85.05, kernel 5.15.0-1085. I've opened internal ticket INF-4521 to track firmware/driver correlation.

mike: devex: ramping up fallback quantized model on hosted API route `/v1/generate` -> set model_alias to `redwood/small-qa-quant` for customers above threshold. quick patch applied to routing rules.

ashley: monitoring: p50 latency recovered partially, error rate down from 6% to 1.2% after draining and routing shift. customers with active sessions may still see failures for a short window.

lee: after drain, other nodes in same rack show increased kernel messages about `watchdog: soft lockup` but haven't crashed yet. recommending to proactively cordon remaining at-risk nodes and rotate them through reboot+firmware update during maintenance window.

tom: agreed. for now prioritize customer-facing mitigation; long term we should blacklist the problematic BIOS rev via nodeSelector or image tag. I'll coordinate with hw-team for firmware push.

support-bot: Noting affected customers list exported to CC-1248; will send status update at T+30m.

ashley: quick checklist before we move to monitoring-only: confirm dedicated pool scaled (mike?), confirm routing policy applied (ashley), confirm no new NotReady spikes for 10m.

mike: dedicated pool +3 instances active and registered, capacity increased by ~35%. autoscaler logs: `nodes registered: 3 -> 6`.

ashley: routing policy applied, tests show new sessions prefer usw-2.

lee: watching kubelet logs — no new crashes for 8m, but dmesg still shows occasional `NVRM: Xid 31` on one node; flagged for firmware.

tom: starting staging repro now with load generator — will report back within 40m.

rosa: documenting mitigation steps in the runbook: add step to detect `watchdog` + `NVRM Xid` signature and auto-isolate nodes before kubelet churn. filing a PR to infra-runbooks.

ashley: closing pager for now, keeping channel open for updates. I'll switch to monitoring and escalate if we see >2 new flaps. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Pager closed by ashley at 4812340155. Incident remains in monitoring state.
